stem: Why is head circumference monitoring most relevant during the first two years of life?

options.text: Because the brain stops growing completely after age 2
Because the cranial sutures remain open, allowing the head to act as a pressure valve
Because measuring a toddler's head is easier than measuring an infant's head
Because hair growth is minimal during this period
Because skull bones are fused and no longer change after birth

explanation: Open cranial sutures make head circumference a useful marker of changes in intracranial volume during early childhood.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because brain growth continues well beyond 2 years, although the rate of growth slows.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because open cranial sutures allow changes in intracranial volume to be reflected in head circumference, so the skull can accommodate growth and raised pressure.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the value of head circumference monitoring is related to skull development, not ease of measurement.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because hair growth does not determine the clinical usefulness of head circumference measurement.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because skull sutures are not fused at birth and remain open during infancy and early childhood.

source.hint: Consider the anatomical state of the skull bones during early childhood.
